Publisher/catalog descriptions and Publishers Weekly plot-summary grammar were treated as discovery or nondiagnostic rather than person evidence.
person_note: The only diagnostic Goodreads event quote uses a participating narratorial 'I'; the other event excerpts are unmarked, while speech, aphorisms, and the historical afterword are non-base material. A sustained publisher extract independently shows Luba and Eliza narrating as 'I', and whole-book structural sources establish that Sofya, Eliza, Varinka, and Luba all supply first-person sections. Because every controlling narrator uses the same grammatical person, the changing narrators and chapter perspectives yield FIRST rather than ALTERNATING. No credible evidence of sustained second- or third-person base narration was found.
